label: SIMULATION RESULTS
disclaimer: All results are produced from placeholder-provenance parameters. They exercise the decision problem and the pipeline only and must NOT be presented as real facility performance. No real customer data exists anywhere in this pipeline.

regenerate.3_export_bundle: uv run --no-sync python -m nxt_range_viewer --out reports/demo_bundle --scenario demand_spike --policy demand_forecast_dispatch --seed 101 --benchmark-report reports/range_agent_e1/report.json

determinism_note: The same (scenario, policy, seed) always regenerates identical frames, events, and KPIs; the only environment-dependent field is the meta.git_commit provenance stamp.

highlights.what_to_say: An unforecast walk-in group hits mid-afternoon: demand jumps from ~20 to ~50 balls/min (peak 52.8/min at 15:07). The spike is deliberately absent from the forecast the AI sees - it has to react, not cheat.

The dispatcher panel narrates each decision live: the policy reads the sensed inventory pipeline against the forecast, detects the shortfall, and staffs collection - every directive re-validated by the safety shield.
Both available robots cycle collect-and-handoff on the map (amber decision lines, trails). A dock failure at 15:26 is retried and absorbed without human help.
Dispenser inventory bottoms out at 1,578 balls at 15:28 - and recovers. The washer loop is kept fed, climbing back above 2,200 by 16:00 and staying positive to close.
Full-day result: 0.0 stockout minutes, 20,751 of 20,751 demanded balls served, 100% service availability, one human assist all day. SIMULATION RESULTS - placeholder parameters, real decision problem.

bonus_beat.what_to_say: Optional: R1 hard-fails in the evening (red ring on the map), the dispatcher requests human assistance, and the robot is recovered in 12 simulated minutes.
